lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Keisha, it's Ana from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've had more energy, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the soda swap went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 1.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My granddaughter is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the soda swap going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My health is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Getting back to work is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that letting go of the Coke keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It was a long weekend with family, you know how it is. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Family time comes first, and food is a big part of that.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That took effort.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can do water at lunch, maybe not dinner yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've got a plan in mind already.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to swap soda for water on 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 7 and not a 4?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 1 out of 4 days, the hard part was letting go of the Coke, and next week you're going to swap soda for water on 4 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Keisha, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Invites agenda, though phrased as yes/no-style
Notices improved energy; benefit of change
Reports one day of swap; a step taken
Need to act; does not want cancer back
Feels better about self; doctor support
Passed over change talk without exploring it
Enjoys food; resists change due to age
Reframes ambivalence: cares, but Coke is hard to give up
Family meals make skipping soda hard
Adds judgment-like framing about family priority
Reflects openness and need for real-life fit
Verbatim repeat of line 10; poorly fitted to 'I don't know'
Plans night before; confidence in method
Past success as reason for confidence
Names barrier and plan to address it
Summary of week and next-step goal

flags.reason: Coach repeats line 10 verbatim after participant said 'I don't know', so it does not track what was said.
After participant's 'My health is why I'm doing this', coach jumped to 'Whatever you pick is fine' instead of exploring the motivation.
Participant said 'too tired for this right now'; coach moved straight to the soda plan without exploring fatigue or readiness.

score.summary: Coach used good autonomy-supporting language and asked useful open questions that drew out many change-talk statements, and the session closed with a clear goal, a confidence rating, barrier planning and a summary. However, coach passed over several change-talk moments (lines 22-23) and fatigue (line 14), and repeated lines verbatim (lines 45, 51), which reduced the sense of empathic listening.
strengths: Line 19: asked permission ('Do you mind if I tell you...') before offering the seltzer idea.
Line 36 and 23: stressed the participant's control over the plan ('It's completely your call').
Line 62: 'Why a 7 and not a 4?' drew out the participant's own confidence reasons.
Line 66: clear summary that checked accuracy before closing.
coaching_tips: Line 14: when the participant says 'too tired for this right now', pause and ask what the tiredness is like before moving to goals.
Line 23: after 'My health is why I'm doing this' (line 22), reflect the motivation and ask what it would mean to act on it, rather than moving on.
Lines 45 and 51: vary your reflections so they match what the participant just said instead of repeating earlier lines.
Line 57: 'I already told my family' is a commitment; reflect it and ask how that support could help before setting the goal.
